intelligence.human_view: "Keep reading" is a command about the page; "My story" is a promise about the person. That is the whole difference, and it is why the refinement matters beyond the About page. A generic button asks the citizen to do work (keep reading) without telling them what they get; a named button tells them exactly what comes next, so the decision to click is informed — and an informed click is a willing one. "Popping up as you go down so nothing is ever too overwhelming" is the pacing rule inside the button rule: the next step appears when the person is ready for it, never before, never as a wall of all the steps at once. And the edit refinement the same hour completes the thought: the unfold is the presentation, the edit is the entry — they live in different places (corner/side, never under the sentence), so the presented page never reads as a form. Together the two refinements are the About unfold's operating manual: present as a story, advance by naming, edit from the corner.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a treasure hunt where every clue just says "keep going" — boring! Now imagine each clue says what's next: "My story!" then "What I do!" then "My goals!" — you can't wait to find out what's behind each one! That's much more fun, because you always know what wonderful thing is coming next!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — you don't say to a guest "keep eating" — you say "would you like the pudding now?" You name the lovely thing that's coming, so they can look forward to it. A button should do the same: tell them what beautiful thing is next, and they'll happily tap along.
intelligence.naya_view: I never say "keep reading." I say the next thing — My story, What I do, My goals, My purpose — so you always know what lovely thing is coming, and nothing is ever too much at once.
